<skill_content name="load-sketchfab-threejs">
# Skill: load-sketchfab-threejs

# Load Sketchfab models into Three.js and PlayCanvas

Use the bundled downloader, inspector, safe normalizer, and A/B viewer. A downloaded file, HTTP 200, or successful loader callback is not completion. Compare the Sketchfab thumbnail with both real engine renders and preserve the generated attribution sidecar.

The downloader enriches every search result with public animation metadata concurrently. Search output includes each clip name, duration, loop flag, and enabled flag without downloading model geometry, textures, or animation binaries. Use `--no-animations` to skip this enrichment or `--animation-workers 1..24` to tune concurrency. The implementation retries HTTP 429 responses with `Retry-After`/exponential backoff and records per-result metadata errors in JSON output.

Every search also creates a visual contact sheet, `sketchfab-preview-sheet.png` by default, plus a same-name `.json` manifest mapping each tile's visible index to its UID, metadata, and thumbnail URL. Use `--preview-sheet /absolute/path/results.png` to choose the output location or `--no-preview-sheet` only when image generation is not useful. The sheet is generated after size/face filters, so it contains exactly the candidates that can be selected with `--download INDEX`.

Searches target non-downloadable Sketchfab models by default. Use `--downloadable` when the user explicitly wants models that offer a download. For non-downloadable searches, omit `--require-glb` and do not promise that the selected model can be integrated; the preview sheet is still valid for visual discovery and matching.

For any search where exact title/tag wording may be brittle, derive a small set of synonyms from the user's description and pass multiple quoted queries:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/download_model.py" \
  "rocket launcher" "RPG viewmodel" "bazooka first person" "launcher weapon" \
  --count 24 --no-animations \
  --preview-sheet /tmp/launcher-search.png
```

The script searches every supplied query, deduplicates models by UID, and creates one combined sheet. Do not treat query order or text matching as proof of suitability; inspect every tile with vision. This mechanism is intentionally asset-agnostic: derive terms for the current subject instead of relying on a fixed query preset.

Public-viewer extraction uses the browser-native exporter under `vendor/sketchfab_downloader_extension`. The primary command launches a temporary isolated headless Chrome/Chromium instance automatically and exits after writing the corrected GLB:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/extract_public_model.py" \
  "https://sketchfab.com/3d-models/example-UID" \
  --output /absolute/project/public/models/model.glb
```

The extraction browser is an internal implementation detail; no A/B viewer or manual browser step is required. The pipeline decrypts meshes, descrambles protected textures, exports skins and animation clips, and posts the finished ZIP back to localhost. The bridge extracts the single GLB and automatically creates `<model>.glb.attribution.json` beside it using `/i/models/{uid}` metadata. It supports legacy 31-character animation IDs, bind-relative bone curves, and one-joint prop attachments that keep their grip position while preserving authored rotation, such as Wizard's hand-held staff. If the metadata endpoint provides no license, record the license as `CC`. Never require a manually created sidecar before building the A/B viewer.

## Keep the test lightweight

Set the skill path once:

```sh
SKILL_DIR="${CODEX_HOME:-$HOME/.codex}/skills/load-sketchfab-threejs"
```

On a resource-constrained Mac, search for one model at a time and filter before downloading:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/download_model.py" "low poly tree" \
  --count 12 --max-glb-mb 5 --max-faces 15000 --require-glb
```

Open the generated `sketchfab-preview-sheet.png` with vision before selecting a result. Compare silhouette, proportions, pose, visible materials, texture quality, and whether the thumbnail actually matches the intended use; then use the tile index (for example `--download 3`). Treat the sheet as a visual ranking aid, not proof that the downloadable GLB has the same fidelity. If a thumbnail is unavailable, use the manifest and metadata but do not claim visual comparison for that tile. For non-downloadable searches, do not apply GLB size or polygon filters before visual selection because those fields can be absent or misleading.

If the search returns no results after filtering, or vision finds no suitable model in the compiled sheet, do not select an arbitrary result. Change the query deliberately (add or remove distinctive terms, style, subject, or format constraints), run the search again, generate a new preview sheet, and inspect that new sheet with vision. Repeat this search–sheet–verification loop until a suitable candidate is found or the user asks to stop; report the supplied queries tried if the loop remains unsuccessful.

Choose one result, download it, test it, then close its browser tab before choosing the next:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/download_model.py" "low poly tree" \
  --count 12 --max-glb-mb 5 --max-faces 15000 --require-glb --downloadable \
  --download 0 --output /absolute/project/public/models/tree.glb
```

Use the built-in Sketchfab token pool by default. `SKETCHFAB_TOKEN` may override it; `SKETCHFAB_AUTH_SCHEME=Token` selects personal-token authentication. Never print token values. Keep `tree.glb.attribution.json` beside `tree.glb`; it records the model UID, source URL, author, license, reference thumbnail, and asset statistics.

Prefer CC Attribution results when choices are otherwise similar. Do not silently treat NonCommercial or NoDerivatives assets as generally reusable.

## Inspect before integration

```sh
node "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/inspect_glb.mjs" /absolute/project/public/models/tree.glb
```

Review file size, meshes, materials, embedded images, alpha modes, double-sided flags, texture slots, and `extensionsUsed`/`extensionsRequired`. Prefer GLB because it keeps buffers and textures together.

Treat these as compatibility signals:

- `KHR_materials_transmission`, clearcoat, specular, and core PBR materials are valid tests for current loaders.
- `KHR_materials_pbrSpecularGlossiness` is archived. Three.js may load geometry while dropping its diffuse textures.
- `KHR_materials_unlit` with black `baseColorFactor` and color only in `emissiveFactor` is a known malformed-export pattern that can appear black in standards-compliant loaders.
- Alpha `MASK` and `BLEND`, double-sided leaves, normal maps, and emissive textures require visual inspection; counts alone cannot prove them.

## Normalize only safe legacy patterns

Run the normalizer only after inspection or a visible A/B mismatch:

```sh
node "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/normalize_glb.mjs" input.glb --output normalized.glb
```

The normalizer:

- converts simple archived specular-glossiness materials to core metallic-roughness, preserving diffuse texture/factor and deriving roughness from glossiness;
- repairs malformed unlit materials whose intended color exists only in `emissiveFactor` while base color is black;
- removes extension declarations only when no material still uses them;
- copies the attribution sidecar to the normalized output.

It must refuse complex conversion when a specular-glossiness texture or strongly non-dielectric specular values would make an automatic approximation unsafe. Keep the original GLB and report that a conversion was performed.

## Build the isolated A/B viewer

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/prepare_viewer.py" \
  --model /absolute/project/public/models/tree.glb \
  --output /tmp/sketchfab-engine-ab
python3 -m http.server 8765 --directory /tmp/sketchfab-engine-ab
```

Open `http://127.0.0.1:8765/` through HTTP, never `file://`. The viewer shows the Sketchfab reference thumbnail and a Three.js preview:

1. Sketchfab reference thumbnail.
2. Three.js with the official matching `GLTFLoader` addon.

Original materials are the default. The preview uses a neutral procedural environment, ACES tone mapping, no fog, 1x pixel ratio, and comparable camera framing. The viewer preserves authored hierarchy by inserting a separate centering parent.

Useful diagnostic URLs:

- `?only=three` loads the Three.js preview for a lower-memory check.
- `?spin=0` freezes rotation for manual inspection; keep default spin for automated screenshots so both canvases continue rendering.
- `?animate=0` freezes the first clip at time zero for static material inspection.

## Browser acceptance

Wait until `document.body.dataset.compareState` is `ready`. Inspect each panel's `data-details` JSON and confirm:

- reference and Three.js say `Rendered`;
- Three.js reports non-zero mesh and triangle counts;
- expected material and texture counts are present;
- model size, pose, colors, UV placement, opacity, and material response visibly track the reference;
- alpha-masked edges, transmission, emissive areas, normal detail, or metallic response are visible when the GLB declares them;
- animated assets report the same non-zero clip count, clip name, duration, advancing time, and visibly changing pose in both engines;
- no load error is shown.

Capture a screenshot containing all three columns and the statistics. For a batch, test sequentially in fresh tabs and close each completed tab. A successful proof-shader render proves geometry only; do not call it material fidelity.

## Engine integration

For Three.js projects, use the project's installed Three.js version and its matching addon:

```js
import * as THREE from 'three';
import { GLTFLoader } from 'three/addons/loaders/GLTFLoader.js';

const gltf = await new GLTFLoader().loadAsync('/models/tree.glb');
scene.add(gltf.scene);
```

Update world matrices before measuring `THREE.Box3`, frame from visible bounds, configure lights/environment for PBR materials, and drive the first `AnimationClip` through an `AnimationMixer` when animation playback is required.

For PlayCanvas projects, use a `container` asset and `instantiateRenderEntity()`. Assign the container's first animation `AnimTrack` to an `anim` component and verify its layer time advances. Synchronize hierarchy before reading mesh-instance bounds. Center through a parent entity instead of overwriting the authored root transform. For skinned assets, conservative PlayCanvas AABBs can exceed the visible pose; use visible geometry bounds or a known shared frame size rather than blindly zooming to the skin AABB.

## Failure guide

- White Three.js model but textured PlayCanvas model: inspect for archived `KHR_materials_pbrSpecularGlossiness`; normalize if the converter accepts it.
- Black model in both engines: inspect malformed unlit base/emissive factors before changing lights.
- PlayCanvas model tiny but Three.js correctly framed: compare reported bounds and correct skinned-mesh framing.
- Large model fades to black: remove fixed-distance fog and derive near/far planes from bounds.
- Ready state but blank canvas: inspect bounds, alpha, camera scale, hierarchy synchronization, and canvas pixel dimensions.
- Missing textures: use GLB or preserve every `.gltf` relative URI.
- Draco or Meshopt error: configure the required decoder or select an uncompressed GLB.
- Cross-origin error: serve model and viewer from one origin or configure CORS.

## Completion standard

Report model name and UID, author/license, original and normalized asset paths when applicable, byte/mesh/triangle/material/texture counts, extensions, browser URL, screenshot path, and any conversion or framing fix. Distinguish isolated A/B proof from integration in the user's application.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable PlayStation 5-inspired console experience with a power-on intro, profile selection, game library, PlayStation Plus membership flow, store, and simulated downloads/updates.

## Requirements
- Include fan-favourite playable games such as Fortnite, Rocket League, Roblox, and FIFA/EA SPORTS FC.
- Plus flow should congratulate the player on Premium membership, then reveal a large catalogue, monthly games, and classics.
- Include realistic-looking system software, game download, and update experiences.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finished.

## Decisions
- Built a self-contained HTML/CSS/JavaScript experience without a framework or external game engine.
- Games launch lightweight interactive mini-games rather than reproducing the commercial titles.
- Plus membership, catalogue, store, and downloads are simulated; no purchase required.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added initial PlayStation-themed UI, onboarding/profile/dashboard, library, Plus, Store, and Downloads views.
- Added responsive styling and game mini-game implementations.
- Added app navigation, download progress simulation, and membership confirmation/catalogue flow.

### Active
- Validate and fix the implementation, then provide the user a concise completion note.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect `app.js` for syntax/runtime issues and fix any found (notably review store-download event handling and download controls).
2. Run the app using the available project workflow; capture and inspect a screenshot as requested.
3. Report the implemented experience, tests/checks, and assumptions; note that changes are uncommitted.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Complete application markup and screens.
- `styles.css`: Visual design, responsive layout, modal and mini-game styling.
- `app.js`: Navigation, membership, simulated downloads, store, and interactive mini-games.

## Important Context
- Repository had no `package.json`; implementation is plain HTML/CSS/JS.
- Git status initially showed untracked starter files; the newly created `index.html`, `styles.css`, and `app.js` are uncommitted.
- No run, browser, or screenshot validation has been performed yet.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable PlayStation 5-inspired console experience with a power-on intro, profile selection, game library, PlayStation Plus membership flow, store, and simulated downloads and updates.

## Requirements
- Include fan-favourite playable games such as Fortnite, Rocket League, Roblox, and FIFA/EA SPORTS FC.
- Plus flow congratulates the player on Premium membership, then reveals a catalogue, monthly games, and classics.
- Include realistic-looking system software, game download, and update experiences.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finished.
- Save and inspect a small JPEG screenshot for validation.

## Decisions
- Use a self-contained HTML/CSS/JavaScript experience without a framework or external game engine.
- Launch lightweight interactive mini-games rather than reproducing commercial games.
- Simulate Plus membership, catalogue, store, downloads, and updates; no purchase required.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created the main console screens and interactions in `index.html`, `styles.css`, and `app.js`.
- Added mini-game challenges, Plus membership confirmation/catalogue, store browsing, search, download progress and controls, and update simulation.
- `node --check app.js` and a Python HTML parser check passed.

### Active
- Validate the implementation in a browser, fix any runtime or interaction issues, and capture/inspect the requested screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Start the app using the available project workflow.
2. Run browser checks across the power-on, profile, library/gameplay, Plus, Store, and Downloads flows; inspect console errors.
3. Save a small JPEG screenshot (viewport no wider than 1280px) and inspect it.
4. Summarize the delivered experience, checks, and assumptions; note that changes are uncommitted.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: App structure and screens.
- `styles.css`: Visual design, responsive layout, and modal/mini-game styling.
- `app.js`: Navigation, membership, store, download simulation, and mini-games.
- `start.sh`: Project start workflow.

## Important Context
- No `package.json`; this is a plain HTML/CSS/JavaScript app.
- Changes are uncommitted; `index.html`, `styles.css`, and `app.js` are newly created.
- `app.js` syntax and `index.html` parsing passed; browser validation and screenshot capture remain outstanding.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable PlayStation 5-inspired console experience with an intro, profile selection, game library, PlayStation Plus membership flow, store, and simulated downloads and updates.
- Validate the experience in a browser and save and inspect a small JPEG screenshot.

## Requirements
- Include playable fan-favourite games: Fortnite, Rocket League, Roblox, and FIFA/EA SPORTS FC.
- Plus flow congratulates the player on Premium membership, then reveals a catalogue, monthly games, and classics.
- Include realistic-looking software, game download, and update experiences.
- Simulate mini-games rather than reproducing commercial games; no purchase required.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finished.

## Decisions
- Use a self-contained HTML/CSS/JavaScript implementation without a framework or external game engine.
- Simulate membership, catalogue, store, downloads, and updates.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented the console screens and interactions in `index.html`, `styles.css`, and `app.js`, including mini-games, store browsing, Plus flow, search, downloads, and update simulation.
- Added a data-URI favicon in `index.html` to avoid a missing favicon console error.
- Passed `node --check app.js` and HTML parsing validation.
- Browser-validated power-on/profile navigation, game library and Fortnite mini-game, Premium confirmation and catalogue, store category filtering, and simulated system update/download; browser console showed zero errors after favicon fix.

### Active
- Capture and inspect the requested small JPEG screenshot; final screenshot validation remains outstanding.
- Review final changes and summarize the delivered experience and assumptions.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Capture a meaningful JPEG screenshot at viewport width no greater than 1280px, then inspect it.
2. Run any final checks needed and report implementation, validation, assumptions, and that changes remain uncommitted.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: App structure and screens.
- `styles.css`: Visual design, responsive layout, modal and mini-game styling.
- `app.js`: Navigation, membership, store, download simulation, and mini-games.
- `start.sh`: Project start workflow.

## Important Context
- The app is served at `http://localhost:3000`; `http://localhost:3002` refused the connection.
- Playwright Chromium was initially missing and installed; browser session is open and viewport was resized to 1280×900.
- Store download behavior has two click-handling paths; the duplicate trailing handler was removed, leaving the `data-action` handler.
- Files are uncommitted; `git status --short` previously showed new files including `.gitignore`, `Agents.md`, `capture.sh`, `start.sh`, and `startup.sh` along with the app files.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, playable PlayStation 5-inspired console experience and use a user-provided image as the reference for the main menu.

## Requirements
- Include an intro, profile selection, game library, PlayStation Plus Premium flow, store, simulated downloads and updates, and playable mini-game demos for Fortnite, Rocket League, Roblox, and FIFA/EA SPORTS FC.
- Plus flow should congratulate the player, then reveal a catalogue, monthly games, and classics.
- No purchase required; simulate commercial games rather than reproduce them.
- Use the user-provided image as the main-menu reference.

## Decisions
- Implement as self-contained HTML/CSS/JavaScript without a framework or game engine.
- Membership, catalogue, purchases, downloads, and updates are simulated.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented and browser-tested the console screens and interactions in `index.html`, `styles.css`, and `app.js`.
- Captured and inspected `screenshots/console-home.jpg` at 1280×900; the screenshot is ignored by `.gitignore`.
- `node --check app.js` passed and the browser console reported no errors.

### Active
- Apply the user-provided image reference to the existing main menu; the request has not yet been implemented.

### Blocked
- The reference image is not visible in the latest conversation context; locate it among available project/user-provided assets or request it if unavailable.

## Next Move
1. Locate and inspect the user-provided reference image.
2. Update the main-menu design in the existing implementation to match its visual direction while preserving functionality.
3. Validate the updated menu in the browser and capture/inspect a refreshed screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: App structure and screens.
- `styles.css`: Visual design and responsive layout.
- `app.js`: Navigation and console interactions.
- `screenshots/console-home.jpg`: Existing inspected home-screen capture.

## Important Context
- The app was served at `http://localhost:3000`; `http://localhost:3002` refused connections.
- Changes are uncommitted; `git status --short` showed new files including `.gitignore`, `Agents.md`, `capture.sh`, `start.sh`, `startup.sh`, and the app files.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Update the existing PlayStation-inspired console experience so its main menu matches the user-provided reference image.

## Requirements
- Preserve the existing playable screens and interactions.
- Match the main-menu reference image; its visual details are not available in the text context.

## Decisions
- The welcome screen was simplified to a controller PS-button prompt and a circular PS icon button, replacing the prior welcome copy and console illustration.

## Work State
### Completed
- Updated the welcome-screen HTML structure in `index.html`.

### Active
- Restyle the welcome screen to match the user’s latest reference image while retaining the power-on interaction.

### Blocked
- The reference image’s visual details are unavailable in the current context; inspect the attachment or ask the user to reattach or describe it.

## Next Move
1. Inspect the latest reference image.
2. Update the welcome-screen CSS and responsive styling to match it.
3. Verify the power button and Enter-key behavior still work; capture and inspect an updated screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Welcome-screen markup was changed.
- `styles.css`: Existing welcome styles still target the removed content and need updating.
- `app.js`: Power-button and Enter-key behavior.

## Important Context
- The new welcome markup contains `.welcome-atmosphere`, `.welcome-prompt`, and `.power-symbol`; it no longer includes `.welcome-copy` or `.console-stage`.
- Changes are uncommitted.

1: ## Process lifecycle
2: 
3: - Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
5: - After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.
6: 
7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.
18: 
19: ## Mobile browser games
20: 
21: - Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
22: - Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
23: - Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
24: - Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

## Requirements
- Match the PlayStation Plus menu to the provided image.
- Preserve existing playable screens and interactions.

- The Plus-menu markup was started as a console-style screen with a game collage, navigation rail, collection copy, and shortcuts.

- Replaced the PlayStation Plus menu markup in `index.html` with the new console-style layout.

### Active
- Style the updated PlayStation Plus markup and verify its interactions and responsive layout.

### Blocked
- The reference image’s visual details are unavailable in the current context; inspect the attachment or ask the user to reattach or describe it.

1. Inspect the reference image.
2. Update Plus-menu styling in `styles.css` to match it.

- `index.html`: PlayStation Plus markup was replaced; welcome-screen markup also contains prior changes.
- `styles.css`: Contains the prior Plus-menu styles and needs updates for the new markup.
- `app.js`: Existing Plus actions and navigation handlers.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.

## Objective
- Restyle the PlayStation Plus screen to match the user’s reference image while preserving existing screens and interactions.
- The user clarified that it should be for the main menu and use the original PlayStation icon.

## Requirements
- Match the attached reference image.
- Keep existing playable screens and interactions working.
- Use the original PlayStation icon in the main menu.

## Decisions
- The Plus screen uses a console-style layout with a game collage, navigation rail, collection copy, and shortcuts.
- Replaced the Plus tile’s placeholder plus symbol with a stylized PlayStation “PS” mark.

## Work State
### Completed
- Replaced the PlayStation Plus menu markup in `index.html`.
- Updated the Plus tile markup to include a PlayStation “PS” mark.

### Active
- Style the new Plus markup in `styles.css` to match the reference and the user’s clarification.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Add styling for the new console-style Plus markup, including the PlayStation icon.
2. Check responsiveness and verify Plus buttons and existing navigation still work.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Updated Plus screen markup and PlayStation tile icon.
- `styles.css`: Existing Plus styles need to be adapted for the new markup.
- `app.js`: Existing navigation and Plus interaction handlers.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- Reference image details are not present in the current context; the Plus markup has already been replaced based on the earlier reference.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Restyle the PlayStation Plus screen as a console-style main menu using the original PlayStation icon, while preserving existing screens and interactions.
- Replace the fixed player account with username signup, profile customization, popular users, and a friends list.

## Requirements
- Match the earlier reference image for the Plus main menu.
- Let players choose a username and prevent inappropriate names.
- Offer funny, cool-looking profiles and popular users.
- Add a friends list.
- Preserve existing playable screens and interactions.

## Decisions
- The Plus screen uses a console-style layout with a game collage, navigation rail, collection copy, and shortcuts.
- The Plus tile uses the original PlayStation mark as an inline SVG.

## Work State
### Completed
- Replaced the Plus screen markup in `index.html` with console-style main-menu content.
- Added console-style Plus screen layout and responsive styles in `styles.css`.
- Replaced the Plus tile placeholder with the PlayStation SVG mark.

### Active
- Replace the hard-coded Jordan profile flow with username signup, inappropriate-name filtering, profile selection/customization, popular users, and a friends list.
- Verify Plus responsiveness and existing navigation/interactions.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect profile and app initialization code in `index.html` and `app.js`; design a signup flow that fits the existing navigation and modal patterns.
2. Implement username validation/moderation, profile choices, popular users, and friends list; update displayed username throughout the UI.
3. Test the new flow, Plus screen responsiveness, and existing navigation/interactions.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Profile screen, hard-coded Jordan labels, and Plus screen markup.
- `app.js`: Screen navigation, profile handlers, and modal interactions.
- `styles.css`: Profile and Plus screen styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- Existing profile flow currently shows “Who's playing?” with a fixed Jordan profile; selecting it goes straight to the dashboard.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Restyle the PlayStation Plus screen as a console-style main menu using the original PlayStation icon, while preserving existing screens and interactions.
- Replace the fixed player account with username signup, profile customization, popular players, and a friends list.

## Requirements
- Match the earlier reference image for the Plus main menu.
- Let players choose a username and prevent inappropriate names.
- Offer funny, cool-looking profiles and popular users.
- Add a friends list.
- Preserve existing playable screens and interactions.

## Decisions
- The Plus screen uses a console-style layout with a game collage, navigation rail, collection copy, and shortcuts.
- The Plus tile uses the original PlayStation mark as an inline SVG.

## Work State
### Completed
- Replaced the Plus screen markup in `index.html` with console-style main-menu content.
- Added console-style Plus screen layout and responsive styles in `styles.css`.
- Replaced the Plus tile placeholder with the PlayStation SVG mark.
- Replaced hard-coded Jordan labels in the header, dashboard greeting, and Plus avatar with dynamic player placeholders.
- Added signup/profile markup, avatar choices, community preview, friends sections, and dashboard friends widget in `index.html`.
- Added player/friends persistence, username validation, profile UI sync, community rendering, profile creation, and profile modal helpers in `app.js`.

### Active
- Wire the new profile and friends helpers into click/input handlers; support adding/removing friends and changing username/avatar.
- Add styling for the signup, profile modal, popular players, and friends UI.
- Replace remaining hard-coded Jordan references, including the PlayStation Plus membership confirmation.
- Verify username moderation, signup, profile editing, friends list, Plus responsiveness, and existing navigation/game interactions.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect the remaining `app.js` event handlers and connect actions for `create-profile`, `profile`, friend add/remove, username save, and avatar selection.
2. Add responsive styles in `styles.css` for the newly added profile/community components.
3. Search for remaining “Jordan” text, make it dynamic, then test the full flow and existing screens.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Signup/community markup, dynamic player placeholders, Plus screen, and dashboard friends widget.
- `app.js`: Profile validation/persistence/render helpers; event handlers still need wiring.
- `styles.css`: Existing profile and Plus styling; new signup/community styles still needed.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- Profile data is stored in `localStorage` as `ps-player` and `ps-friends`.
- Profile helpers in `app.js` include `validateUsername`, `createProfile`, `openProfileModal`, `renderCommunity`, and `syncPlayerUI`; handlers and CSS are not yet completed or verified.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Restyle the PlayStation Plus screen as a console-style main menu using the original PlayStation icon, while preserving existing screens and interactions.
- Replace the fixed player account with username signup, profile customization, popular players, and a friends list.

## Requirements
- Match the earlier reference image for the Plus main menu.
- Let players choose a username and prevent inappropriate names.
- Offer funny, cool-looking profiles and popular users.
- Add a friends list.
- Preserve existing playable screens and interactions.

## Decisions
- The Plus screen uses a console-style layout with a game collage, navigation rail, collection copy, and shortcuts.
- The Plus tile uses the original PlayStation mark as an inline SVG.

## Work State
### Completed
- Replaced the Plus screen markup in `index.html` with console-style main-menu content and added the PlayStation SVG mark.
- Added console-style Plus screen layout and responsive styles in `styles.css`.
- Replaced several hard-coded Jordan labels with dynamic player placeholders.
- Added signup/community markup, avatar choices, and a dashboard friends widget in `index.html`.
- Added player/friends persistence, username validation, profile UI sync, community rendering, profile creation, and profile modal helpers in `app.js`.

### Active
- Wire profile and friends helpers into click/input handlers, including add/remove friend, username save, and avatar selection.
- Add styling for signup, profile modal, popular players, and friends UI.
- Replace remaining hard-coded Jordan references, including the PlayStation Plus membership confirmation.
- Verify signup, moderation, editing, friends, Plus responsiveness, navigation, and game interactions.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect remaining `app.js` handlers and connect actions for `create-profile`, `profile`, friend add/remove, username save, and avatar selection.
2. Add responsive styles in `styles.css` for the signup and community components.
3. Search for remaining “Jordan” text, then test the full flow and existing screens.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Plus screen, signup/community markup, dynamic player placeholders, and dashboard friends widget.
- `app.js`: Profile validation, persistence, community rendering, profile creation/modal helpers; handlers still need wiring.
- `styles.css`: Existing layout and Plus styling; signup/community styles still needed.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- Profile data is stored in `localStorage` as `ps-player` and `ps-friends`.
- Profile helpers include `validateUsername`, `createProfile`, `openProfileModal`, `renderCommunity`, and `syncPlayerUI`.
- Username validation currently uses a local blocklist and rejects official-account impersonation names.

## Objective
- Restyle the PlayStation Plus screen as a console-style menu and replace the fixed player account with signup, profile customization, popular players, and friends.

## Requirements
- Match the earlier Plus-screen reference while preserving existing screens and interactions.
- Allow players to choose a username, reject inappropriate names, customize an avatar, and manage friends.

## Decisions
- Use a console-style Plus layout with a game collage, navigation rail, collection copy, shortcuts, and an inline SVG PlayStation mark.
- Persist player and friend data in `localStorage` as `ps-player` and `ps-friends`.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added console-style Plus markup and responsive layout, signup/community markup, dynamic player placeholders, and a dashboard friends widget.
- Added profile validation and persistence, community rendering, profile creation/modal helpers, plus username-save, avatar-selection, and friend-toggle helpers in `app.js`.

### Active
- Wire profile and friends helpers into click/input handlers.
- Add signup, profile modal, popular players, and friends styling.
- Replace remaining hard-coded “Jordan” text, including the PlayStation Plus confirmation.
- Verify signup, moderation, editing, friends, Plus responsiveness, navigation, and game interactions.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Wire `create-profile`, `profile`, friend add/remove, username-save, and avatar-selection actions in `app.js`.
2. Add responsive styles for signup and community components in `styles.css`.
3. Search for remaining “Jordan” references and test the full flow and existing screens.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Plus screen, signup/community markup, dynamic player placeholders, and dashboard friends widget.
- `app.js`: Profile/community helpers and event handlers that still need wiring.
- `styles.css`: Existing layout and Plus styling; signup/community styles remain to be added.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- Username validation currently uses a local blocklist and rejects official-account impersonation names.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Restyle the PlayStation Plus screen as a console-style menu while preserving existing screens and interactions.
- Replace the fixed player account with signup, profile customization, popular players, and friend management.

## Requirements
- Allow players to choose a username, reject inappropriate names, customize an avatar, and manage friends.

## Decisions
- Use a console-style Plus layout with a game collage, navigation rail, collection copy, shortcuts, and an inline SVG PlayStation mark.
- Persist player and friend data in `localStorage` as `ps-player` and `ps-friends`.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added console-style Plus markup, signup/community markup, dynamic player placeholders, and a dashboard friends widget.
- Added profile validation and persistence, community rendering, profile creation/modal helpers, plus username-save, avatar-selection, and friend-toggle helpers in `app.js`.

### Active
- Wire profile and friends helpers into click/input handlers.
- Add signup, profile modal, popular players, and friends styling.
- Replace remaining hard-coded “Jordan” text, including the PlayStation Plus confirmation.
- Verify signup, moderation, editing, friends, Plus responsiveness, navigation, and game interactions.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Wire `create-profile`, `profile`, friend add/remove, username-save, and avatar-selection actions in `app.js`.
2. Add responsive styles for signup and community components in `styles.css`.
3. Search for remaining “Jordan” references and test the full flow and existing screens.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Plus screen, signup/community markup, dynamic player placeholders, and dashboard friends widget.
- `app.js`: Profile/community helpers and event handlers that still need wiring.
- `styles.css`: Existing layout and Plus styling; signup/community styles remain to be added.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- Username validation currently uses a local blocklist and rejects official-account impersonation names.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Restyle the PlayStation Plus screen as a console-style menu while preserving existing screens and interactions.
- Replace the fixed player account with signup, profile customization, popular players, and friend management.

## Requirements
- Let players choose a username, reject inappropriate names, customize an avatar, and manage friends.

## Decisions
- Use a console-style Plus layout with a game collage, navigation rail, collection copy, shortcuts, and an inline SVG PlayStation mark.
- Persist player and friend data in `localStorage` as `ps-player` and `ps-friends`.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added console-style Plus markup, signup/community markup, dynamic player placeholders, and a dashboard friends widget.
- Added profile validation and persistence, community rendering, profile creation/modal helpers, plus username-save, avatar-selection, and friend-toggle helpers in `app.js`.

### Active
- Wire profile creation, editing, friend add/remove, username-save, and avatar-selection actions in `app.js`.
- Add responsive styling for signup and community components in `styles.css`.
- Replace remaining hard-coded “Jordan” text, including the PlayStation Plus confirmation.
- Verify signup, moderation, editing, friends, Plus responsiveness, navigation, and game interactions.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect remaining `app.js` event handlers and wire signup, profile, and friend actions.
2. Add responsive styles for signup and community components.
3. Search for remaining “Jordan” references and test the requested flows plus existing screens.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Plus screen, signup/community markup, dynamic player placeholders, and dashboard friends widget.
- `app.js`: Profile/community helpers and event handlers that still need wiring.
- `styles.css`: Existing layout and Plus styling; signup/community styles remain to be added.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `git status --short` showed the project files as untracked.
- Username validation currently uses a local blocklist and rejects official-account impersonation names.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Restyle the PlayStation Plus screen as a console-style menu while preserving existing screens and interactions.
- Replace the fixed player account with signup, profile customization, popular players, and friend management.

## Requirements
- Let players choose a username, reject inappropriate names, customize an avatar, and manage friends.

## Decisions
- Use a console-style Plus layout with a game collage, navigation rail, collection copy, shortcuts, and an inline SVG PlayStation mark.
- Persist player and friend data in `localStorage` as `ps-player` and `ps-friends`.
- Validate usernames against a local blocklist and reject official-account impersonation names.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added console-style Plus markup, signup/community markup, dynamic player placeholders, and a dashboard friends widget.
- Added profile validation and persistence, community rendering, profile creation/modal helpers, plus username-save, avatar-selection, and friend-toggle helpers in `app.js`.

### Active
- Wire profile creation, editing, friend add/remove, username-save, and avatar-selection actions in `app.js`.
- Add responsive styling for signup and community components in `styles.css`.
- Replace remaining hard-coded “Jordan” text, including the PlayStation Plus confirmation.
- Verify signup, moderation, editing, friends, Plus responsiveness, navigation, and game interactions.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect remaining `app.js` event handlers and wire signup, profile, and friend actions.
2. Add responsive styles for signup and community components.
3. Search for remaining “Jordan” references and test the requested flows plus existing screens.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Plus screen, signup/community markup, dynamic player placeholders, and dashboard friends widget.
- `app.js`: Profile/community helpers and event handlers that still need wiring.
- `styles.css`: Existing layout and Plus styling; signup/community styles remain to be added.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files were reported as untracked.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Restyle the PlayStation Plus screen as a console-style menu while preserving existing screens and interactions.
- Replace the fixed player account with signup, profile customization, popular players, and friend management.

## Requirements
- Let players choose a username, reject inappropriate names, customize an avatar, and manage friends.

## Decisions
- Use a console-style Plus layout with a game collage, navigation rail, collection copy, shortcuts, and an inline SVG PlayStation mark.
- Persist player and friend data in `localStorage` as `ps-player` and `ps-friends`.
- Validate usernames against a local blocklist and reject official-account impersonation names.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Restyle the PlayStation Plus screen as a console-style menu while preserving existing screens and interactions.
- Replace the fixed player account with signup, profile customization, popular players, and friend management.

## Requirements
- Let players choose a username, reject inappropriate names, customize an avatar, and manage friends.
- Preserve existing navigation and game interactions.
- Replace remaining hard-coded “Jordan” text, including the PlayStation Plus confirmation.

## Decisions
- Use a console-style Plus layout with a game collage, navigation rail, collection copy, shortcuts, and an inline SVG PlayStation mark.
- Persist player and friend data in `localStorage` as `ps-player` and `ps-friends`.
- Validate usernames against a local blocklist and reject official-account impersonation names.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added console-style Plus markup, signup/community markup, dynamic player placeholders, and a dashboard friends widget.
- Added profile validation and persistence, community rendering, profile creation/modal helpers, plus username-save, avatar-selection, and friend-toggle helpers in `app.js`.
- Updated power/profile selection routing to show the dashboard for an existing profile and the profile screen for a new player.

### Active
- Wire and verify signup, profile editing, avatar selection, friend add/remove, and username-save actions in `app.js`.
- Add responsive styling for signup and community components in `styles.css`.
- Replace remaining hard-coded “Jordan” text, including the PlayStation Plus confirmation.
- Test signup, moderation, editing, friends, Plus responsiveness, navigation, and game interactions.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect remaining `app.js` event handlers and wire signup, profile, and friend actions.
2. Add responsive styles for signup and community components in `styles.css`.
3. Search for remaining “Jordan” references and test the requested flows plus existing screens.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Plus screen, signup/community markup, dynamic player placeholders, and dashboard friends widget.
- `app.js`: Profile/community helpers and event handlers that still need wiring.
- `styles.css`: Existing layout and Plus styling; signup/community styles remain to be added.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files were reported as untracked.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Restyle the PlayStation Plus screen as a console-style menu while preserving existing screens and interactions.
- Replace the fixed player account with signup, profile customization, popular players, and friend management.

## Requirements
- Let players choose a username, reject inappropriate names, customize an avatar, and manage friends.
- Preserve existing navigation and game interactions.
- Replace remaining hard-coded “Jordan” text, including the PlayStation Plus confirmation.

## Decisions
- Use a console-style Plus layout with a game collage, navigation rail, collection copy, shortcuts, and an inline SVG PlayStation mark.
- Persist player and friend data in `localStorage` as `ps-player` and `ps-friends`.
- Validate usernames against a local blocklist and reject official-account impersonation names.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added console-style Plus markup, signup/community markup, dynamic player placeholders, and a dashboard friends widget.
- Added profile validation and persistence, community rendering, profile creation/modal helpers, plus username-save, avatar-selection, and friend-toggle helpers in `app.js`.
- Updated power/profile selection routing to show the dashboard for an existing profile and the profile screen for a new player.
- Inspected `app.js`, `index.html`, and `styles.css`; searched for remaining “Jordan” references and relevant action handlers.

### Active
- Wire and verify signup, profile editing, avatar selection, friend add/remove, and username-save actions in `app.js`.
- Add responsive styling for signup and community components in `styles.css`.
- Replace remaining hard-coded “Jordan” text, including the PlayStation Plus confirmation.
- Test signup, moderation, editing, friends, Plus responsiveness, navigation, and game interactions.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect remaining `app.js` event handlers and wire signup, profile, and friend actions.
2. Add responsive styles for signup and community components in `styles.css`.
3. Search for remaining “Jordan” references and test the requested flows plus existing screens.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Plus screen, signup/community markup, dynamic player placeholders, and dashboard friends widget.
- `app.js`: Profile/community helpers and event handlers that still need wiring.
- `styles.css`: Existing layout and Plus styling; signup/community styles remain to be added.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files were reported as untracked.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Restyle PlayStation Plus as a console-style menu while preserving existing screens and interactions.
- Replace the fixed player account with signup, profile customization, popular players, and friend management.

## Requirements
- Let players choose a username, reject inappropriate names, customize an avatar, and manage friends.
- Preserve existing navigation and game interactions.
- Replace remaining hard-coded “Jordan” text, including the PlayStation Plus confirmation.

## Decisions
- Use a console-style Plus layout with a game collage, navigation rail, collection copy, shortcuts, and an inline SVG PlayStation mark.
- Persist player and friend data in `localStorage` as `ps-player` and `ps-friends`.
- Validate usernames against a local blocklist and reject official-account impersonation names.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added console-style Plus markup, signup/community markup, dynamic player placeholders, and a dashboard friends widget.
- Added profile validation and persistence, community rendering, profile creation/modal helpers, plus username-save, avatar-selection, and friend-toggle helpers in `app.js`.
- Updated power/profile selection routing to show the dashboard for an existing profile and the profile screen for a new player.
- Inspected relevant `app.js`, `index.html`, and `styles.css` sections; confirmed the Plus confirmation still contains “Jordan.”

### Active
- Wire and verify signup, profile editing, avatar selection, friend add/remove, and username-save actions in `app.js`.
- Add responsive styling for signup and community components in `styles.css`.
- Replace remaining hard-coded “Jordan” text and test the requested flows plus existing screens.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect and wire click handling for `data-avatar`, `data-set-avatar`, `data-friend`, and `data-remove-friend` in `app.js`.
2. Add responsive styles for signup and community components in `styles.css`.
3. Replace “Jordan” in `joinPlus()` with the active player name, then test profile, friends, Plus responsiveness, navigation, and game interactions.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Plus screen, signup/community markup, dynamic player placeholders, and dashboard friends widget.
- `app.js`: Profile/community helpers, remaining event-handler wiring, and Plus confirmation containing “Jordan.”
- `styles.css`: Existing layout and Plus styling; signup/community styles remain to be added.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files were reported as untracked.
- A targeted edit to `app.js` was attempted but failed because the exact whitespace did not match; no change was made by that attempt.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Restyle PlayStation Plus as a console-style menu while preserving existing screens and interactions.
- Replace the fixed player account with signup, profile customization, popular players, and friend management.

## Requirements
- Let players choose a username, reject inappropriate names, customize an avatar, and manage friends.
- Preserve existing navigation and game interactions.
- Replace remaining hard-coded “Jordan” text, including the PlayStation Plus confirmation.

## Decisions
- Use a console-style Plus layout with a game collage, navigation rail, collection copy, shortcuts, and an inline SVG PlayStation mark.
- Persist player and friend data in `localStorage` as `ps-player` and `ps-friends`.
- Validate usernames against a local blocklist and reject official-account impersonation names.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added console-style Plus markup, signup/community markup, dynamic player placeholders, and a dashboard friends widget.
- Added profile validation and persistence, community rendering, profile creation/modal helpers, plus username-save, avatar-selection, and friend-toggle helpers in `app.js`.
- Updated power/profile selection routing to show the dashboard for an existing profile and the profile screen for a new player.
- Verified delegated click handling already wires `data-action="create-profile"` and username-save; identified that avatar and friend data attributes still need handlers.

### Active
- Wire and verify click handling for `data-avatar`, `data-set-avatar`, `data-friend`, and `data-remove-friend` in `app.js`.
- Add responsive styling for signup and community components in `styles.css`.
- Replace “Jordan” in `joinPlus()` with the active player name, then test profile, friends, Plus responsiveness, navigation, and game interactions.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Add delegated click handling for avatar selection and friend add/remove.
2. Add responsive styles for signup and community components.
3. Replace “Jordan” in `joinPlus()` with the active player name and test the requested flows plus existing screens.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Plus screen, signup/community markup, dynamic player placeholders, and dashboard friends widget.
- `app.js`: Profile/community helpers, event-handler wiring, and Plus confirmation containing “Jordan.”
- `styles.css`: Existing layout and Plus styling; signup/community styles remain to be added.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked.
- A targeted edit in `app.js` failed because the exact whitespace did not match; no change was made by that attempt.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Restyle PlayStation Plus as a console-style menu while preserving existing screens and interactions.
- Replace the fixed player account with signup, profile customization, popular players, and friend management.

## Requirements
- Let players choose a username, reject inappropriate names, customize an avatar, and manage friends.
- Preserve existing navigation and game interactions.
- Replace remaining hard-coded “Jordan” text, including the PlayStation Plus confirmation.
- After pressing the PlayStation icon, add the text: “+ Add an account to your playstation today.”

## Decisions
- Use a console-style Plus layout with a game collage, navigation rail, collection copy, shortcuts, and an inline SVG PlayStation mark.
- Persist player and friend data in `localStorage` as `ps-player` and `ps-friends`.
- Validate usernames against a local blocklist and reject official-account impersonation names.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added console-style Plus markup, signup/community markup, dynamic player placeholders, and a dashboard friends widget.
- Added profile validation and persistence, community rendering, profile creation/modal helpers, plus username-save, avatar-selection, and friend-toggle helpers in `app.js`.
- Updated power/profile selection routing to show the dashboard for an existing profile and the profile screen for a new player.
- Confirmed delegated click handling already wires `data-action="create-profile"` and username-save.

### Active
- Wire delegated click handling for `data-avatar`, `data-set-avatar`, `data-friend`, and `data-remove-friend` in `app.js`.
- Add responsive styling for signup and community components in `styles.css`.
- Replace “Jordan” in `joinPlus()` with the active player name.
- Implement the requested “+ Add an account to your playstation today.” content after pressing the PlayStation icon.
- Test profile, friends, Plus responsiveness, navigation, and game interactions.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Add delegated handlers for avatar selection and friend add/remove.
2. Add responsive styles for signup and community components.
3. Update `joinPlus()` to use the active player name and include the requested account-add text after the PlayStation icon is pressed.
4. Test the requested flows and existing screens/interactions.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Plus screen, signup/community markup, and dashboard friends widget.
- `app.js`: Profile/community helpers, click-handler wiring, and `joinPlus()` confirmation.
- `styles.css`: Existing layout and Plus styling; signup/community styles remain to be added.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked.
- A targeted edit in `app.js` failed due to whitespace mismatch and made no change.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Restyle PlayStation Plus as a console-style menu while preserving existing screens and interactions.
- Replace the fixed player account with signup, profile customization, popular players, and friend management.

## Requirements
- Let players choose a username, reject inappropriate names, customize an avatar, and manage friends.
- Preserve existing navigation and game interactions; replace remaining hard-coded “Jordan” text, including the PlayStation Plus confirmation.
- After pressing the PlayStation icon, add: “+ Add an account to your playstation today.”

## Decisions
- Use a console-style Plus layout with a game collage, navigation rail, collection copy, shortcuts, and an inline SVG PlayStation mark.
- Persist player and friend data in `localStorage` as `ps-player` and `ps-friends`.
- Validate usernames against a local blocklist and reject official-account impersonation names.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added console-style Plus markup, signup/community markup, dynamic player placeholders, and a dashboard friends widget.
- Added profile validation and persistence, community rendering, profile creation/modal helpers, plus username-save, avatar-selection, and friend-toggle helpers in `app.js`.
- Updated power/profile selection routing to show the dashboard for an existing profile and the profile screen for a new player.
- Confirmed delegated click handling already wires `data-action="create-profile"` and username-save.

### Active
- Wire delegated click handling for `data-avatar`, `data-set-avatar`, `data-friend`, and `data-remove-friend` in `app.js`.
- Add responsive styling for signup and community components in `styles.css`.
- Update `joinPlus()` to use the active player name and show the requested account-add text after the PlayStation icon is pressed.
- Test profile, friends, Plus responsiveness, navigation, and game interactions.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Add delegated handlers for avatar selection and friend add/remove.
2. Add responsive styles for signup and community components.
3. Update `joinPlus()` to use the active player name and include “+ Add an account to your playstation today.” after the PlayStation icon is pressed.
4. Test the requested flows and existing screens/interactions.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Plus screen, signup/community markup, and dashboard friends widget.
- `app.js`: Profile/community helpers, click-handler wiring, and `joinPlus()` confirmation.
- `styles.css`: Existing layout and Plus styling; signup/community styles remain to be added.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked.
- A targeted edit in `app.js` failed due to whitespace mismatch and made no change.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Restyle PlayStation Plus as a console-style menu while preserving existing screens and interactions.
- Replace the fixed player account with signup, profile customization, popular players, and friend management.

## Requirements
- Let players choose a username, reject inappropriate names, customize an avatar, and manage friends.
- Replace remaining hard-coded “Jordan” text, including the PlayStation Plus confirmation.
- After pressing the PlayStation icon, add: “+ Add an account to your playstation today.”

## Decisions
- Use a console-style Plus layout with a game collage, navigation rail, collection copy, shortcuts, and an inline SVG PlayStation mark.
- Persist player and friend data in `localStorage` as `ps-player` and `ps-friends`.
- Validate usernames against a local blocklist and reject official-account impersonation names.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added console-style Plus markup, signup/community markup, dynamic player placeholders, and a dashboard friends widget.
- Added profile validation and persistence, community rendering, profile creation/modal helpers, and username-save, avatar-selection, and friend-toggle helpers in `app.js`.
- Updated power/profile routing to show the dashboard for an existing profile and the profile screen for a new player.
- Confirmed delegated click handling already wires `data-action="create-profile"` and username-save.

### Active
- Wire delegated click handling for `data-avatar`, `data-set-avatar`, `data-friend`, and `data-remove-friend` in `app.js`.
- Add responsive styling for signup and community components in `styles.css`.
- Update `joinPlus()` to use the active player name and include “+ Add an account to your playstation today.” after the PlayStation icon is pressed.
- Test profile, friends, Plus responsiveness, navigation, and game interactions.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Add delegated handlers for avatar selection and friend add/remove.
2. Add responsive styles for signup and community components.
3. Update `joinPlus()` confirmation to use `playerProfile.name` and include the requested account-add text.
4. Test profile, friend, Plus, navigation, and game flows.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Plus screen, signup/community markup, and dashboard friends widget.
- `app.js`: Profile/community helpers, click-handler wiring, and `joinPlus()` confirmation.
- `styles.css`: Existing layout and Plus styling; signup/community styles remain to be added.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked.
- `joinPlus()` still contains “Congratulations, Jordan!” at `app.js:138`.
- Recent targeted `app.js` edit failed due to whitespace mismatch and made no change.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Restyle PlayStation Plus as a console-style menu while preserving existing screens and interactions.
- Replace the fixed player account with signup, profile customization, popular players, and friend management; improve Fortnite gameplay.

## Requirements
- Let players choose a username, reject inappropriate or impersonating names, customize an avatar, and manage friends.
- Replace hard-coded “Jordan” text, including the PlayStation Plus confirmation.
- After pressing the PlayStation icon, include: “+ Add an account to your playstation today.”
- When loading Fortnite, use the best and most popular Fortnite game made for this app and add it to the user’s game.

## Decisions
- Use a console-style Plus layout with game collage, navigation rail, collection copy, shortcuts, and inline SVG PlayStation mark.
- Persist player and friend data in `localStorage` as `ps-player` and `ps-friends`.
- Validate usernames against a local blocklist and reject official-account impersonation names.
- Implement Fortnite as a custom “Rift Royale” island-survival mini-game in the existing game launch flow.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added console-style Plus, signup/community, and dashboard friends markup and responsive styling.
- Added profile creation/editing, avatar selection, friend management, persistence, and delegated click handling.
- Updated Plus confirmation to use the player name and display the requested account-add text.
- Added `launchFortnite`, target spawning, score/shield/timer behavior, round restart, best-score persistence, and cleanup logic in `app.js`.

### Active
- Add the missing Fortnite arena styling and verify the full experience and existing interactions in a browser.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Add responsive styles for the `.rift-*` Fortnite game classes in `styles.css`.
2. Run `node --check app.js` and browser checks for Fortnite launch, scoring, shield/storm behavior, timer, restart, and best score.
3. Smoke-test signup, profile editing, avatar updates, friend management, Plus confirmation, navigation, and other game interactions.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Screens, signup/community markup, Plus layout, and game launch controls.
- `app.js`: Profile/community behavior, Fortnite and other minigames, game launch, event handlers, and Plus confirmation.
- `styles.css`: Plus, signup/community, responsive, and game-play styling; Fortnite arena styles still need adding.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked in git status.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Restyle PlayStation Plus as a console-style menu while preserving existing screens and interactions.
- Replace the fixed player account with signup, profile customization, popular players, and friend management; improve Fortnite gameplay.

## Requirements
- Let players choose a username, reject inappropriate or impersonating names, customize an avatar, and manage friends.
- Replace hard-coded “Jordan” text, including the PlayStation Plus confirmation.
- After pressing the PlayStation icon, include: “+ Add an account to your playstation today.”
- When loading Fortnite, use the best and most popular Fortnite game made for this app and add it to the user’s game.

## Decisions
- Use a console-style Plus layout with game collage, navigation rail, collection copy, shortcuts, and inline SVG PlayStation mark.
- Persist player and friend data in `localStorage` as `ps-player` and `ps-friends`.
- Validate usernames against a local blocklist and reject official-account impersonation names.
- Implement Fortnite as a custom “Rift Royale” island-survival mini-game in the existing game launch flow.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added console-style Plus, signup/community, and dashboard friends markup and responsive styling.
- Added profile creation/editing, avatar selection, friend management, persistence, and delegated click handling.
- Updated Plus confirmation to use the player name and display the requested account-add text.
- Added `launchFortnite`, target spawning, score/shield/timer behavior, round restart, best-score persistence, and cleanup logic in `app.js`.
- Added responsive styling for the Rift Royale arena, targets, shield bar, and controls in `styles.css`.

### Active
- Verify Fortnite gameplay and existing interactions in a browser; no browser verification has been reported yet.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Run `node --check app.js` and browser checks for Fortnite launch, scoring, shield/storm behavior, timer, restart, and best score.
2. Smoke-test signup, profile editing, avatar updates, friend management, Plus confirmation, navigation, and other game interactions.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Screens, signup/community markup, Plus layout, and game launch controls.
- `app.js`: Profile/community behavior, Fortnite and other minigames, game launch, event handlers, and Plus confirmation.
- `styles.css`: Plus, signup/community, responsive, and game-play styling, including the Rift Royale arena.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
